subject.title: fix(doctor): warn when maxActiveTranscriptBytes is set without truncateAfterCompaction

question: Should default `openclaw doctor --lint` warn and fail for every positive `maxActiveTranscriptBytes` setting that lacks `truncateAfterCompaction`, despite current documentation treating that configuration as a disabled guard?
rationale: Both outcomes are technically coherent: the warning prevents a silently ineffective setting, while default enablement changes lint behavior for existing documented configurations and automation. The repository needs maintainer intent on the permanent Doctor contract.

options.title: Adopt default warning
options.body: Keep the check enabled by default, update the public compaction documentation to call the combination a misconfiguration, and accept the lint-result compatibility change.

options.title: Make the check opt-in
options.body: Keep the diagnostic available through an explicit Doctor check or stricter lint mode so existing intentional disabled-guard configurations remain clean by default.

recommendation.title: Adopt default warning
recommendation.body: Keep the check enabled by default, update the public compaction documentation to call the combination a misconfiguration, and accept the lint-result compatibility change.

likelyOwner.reason: A compaction/Doctor area owner must set the compatibility policy; the available evidence does not safely identify an individual.
